transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I keep holding on to this belief that my clients and managers are secretly monitoring and using my translations in ways they deny, and nothing anyone says can convince me otherwise. It's the main reason I'm here today, because I just can't seem to shake this conviction no matter what.
Have you noticed any other unusual beliefs, hearing or seeing things that others do not, or is this conviction the only one?

No, I don't hear or see things that aren't there, and this is the only unusual belief I have. My only concern is this specific situation with my clients and how they are secretly monitoring my translations.
Have you ever had any other fixed false beliefs, or any hallucinations like hearing voices or seeing things that other people do not?

No, I have never experienced hallucinations like hearing voices or seeing things. I don't have any other unusual beliefs either, but I want to be clear that what is happening with my translations is not a "false belief." It is absolutely real, and they are definitely monitoring my work.
Is this belief limited only to your clients and managers monitoring your translations, or do you also believe there are other people or situations involved in a similar way?

Yes, it is strictly limited to my work environment—specifically my clients, managers, and the upper management who are orchestrating this monitoring. I don't believe anyone else, like the government or my neighbors, is involved in this at all. The only way it affects others is my wife, who is upset because I've had to turn down promotions and travel to protect myself from their scrutiny.
Has this belief ever spread beyond your work situation, or has it stayed strictly limited to your clients, managers, and translations the whole time?

No, it has never spread beyond my work; it remains strictly limited to my translations, clients, and upper management. It hasn't affected how I interact with neighbors or strangers at all, though it has caused some arguments with my wife. She is quite upset because I've turned down a promotion and avoided certain travel plans that I felt were connected to their monitoring.
How long have you had this belief about your clients and managers monitoring your translations? Has it been present for at least one month, or longer?

It has been going on for about eleven months now, so it is definitely much longer than a month. It all started right after a tense video call where they challenged my translation choices, and it has been constant ever since.
Has this belief caused you to stop working, lose your job, or have major problems in other areas of life, or is it mainly limited to this one work-related situation?

No, I haven't lost my job at all—I'm still working full-time, paying my bills, and managing things at home normally. The only real disruptions are that I've had to turn down a promotion, avoid certain projects and business trips, and deal with the tension that has caused with my wife. Aside from those specific decisions to protect myself from their monitoring, my day-to-day life is completely unaffected.

During the past 11 months, have you had any major changes in mood, such as feeling very depressed, unusually energized, or having other mental health symptoms that started around the same time as this belief?

No, I haven't had any major mood shifts like feeling really depressed or unusually energized. My primary concern and source of stress has simply been the constant worry about being monitored. Aside from that anxiety, my overall mood has remained pretty stable.
Have you ever had any other psychotic symptoms, such as disorganized speech or behavior, or a clear decline in your overall functioning outside of this work-related belief?

No, I have never had disorganized speech or behavior, and my overall functioning has not declined at all. Aside from turning down that promotion and avoiding certain projects to protect myself, I still work full-time, meet my deadlines, and manage my household normally. Outside of those specific decisions, my day-to-day life is completely unaffected.
Besides the work-related decisions you mentioned, has this belief caused you any other problems in your daily life, like trouble sleeping, taking care of yourself, or getting along with other people?

My sleep, self-care, and daily routine are mostly fine, and I still manage to do my work and pay the bills. However, it has caused some interpersonal strain, leading to arguments with my wife over family travel plans and making my interactions with colleagues and clients feel a bit tense. Aside from those strained relationships, my basic day-to-day functioning is completely normal.
Has this belief ever led you to stop working, lose a job, or have major problems in your daily life outside of avoiding certain projects or travel?

No, I have not lost my job or stopped working at all; I am still working full-time and meeting all of my professional deadlines. Aside from turning down that promotion and avoiding certain travel plans to protect myself, my daily life is completely normal, and I still pay my bills and handle things at home without any issues.
Do you ever consider that this belief might be mistaken or that there could be another explanation, even a small one, or are you completely certain it is true?

I am completely certain it is true, and nothing can convince me otherwise. My wife and colleagues tell me it is just routine quality assurance, but I cannot ignore the evidence, like the highly specific phrasing in their emails and the odd timing of their "random" checks. The signs are simply too clear to be a coincidence, so there is no doubt in my mind.
Have you ever used alcohol, recreational drugs, or any medications that could have started around the time this belief began, or have you had any head injury or medical illness that might explain it?

No, I don't drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs, and I'm not taking any medications that could cause this. I also haven't had any head injuries or physical illnesses that could explain what is going on.
Before this started, did you already have a strong, long-standing suspiciousness or belief that people were out to monitor or harm you, or did this belief begin for the first time only 11 months ago?

No, I never held any suspicious beliefs or felt that people were out to monitor or harm me before that. Prior to eleven months ago, I only had some general anxiety about the accuracy and confidentiality of my translation work. This conviction began for the very first time right after that tense video call.

Before this started 11 months ago, did you generally tend to be suspicious, sensitive to criticism, or reluctant to trust other people in other parts of your life? Or was this belief completely new for you?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it much. I've always been a bit anxious about accuracy and confidentiality in my work, but I wouldn't say I had general issues with trust or suspiciousness before this.
Before this started, did you generally tend to be very suspicious or mistrustful of other people in many areas of your life, or was this belief completely new for you?

I've always been an anxious person who values accuracy and confidentiality, but I never had a general mistrust of other people before this. This specific feeling of being monitored and targeted by my clients is entirely new and only started with this job.
